A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SFTMix work. All 12 pages of v2 and 14 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v2 reports original instruction-following and medical QA experiments, ablations, and 200 human preference judgments (Tables 1–9 and Appendix B).

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds model, dataset, baseline, multilingual, and sensitivity evaluations (Table 1 and Appendix A).

M1.justification: The confidence calculation, equal dataset partition, representation/label interpolation, random pairing, and combined NTP–Mixup objective remain unchanged. The defaults remain α = 0.5 and μ = 0.2; mixing extreme thirds is an additional ablation.

E1.justification: v3 adds training on Tulu3-939K and extends the previously English-only evaluation coverage to Chinese and French instruction following, using language-specific Alpaca variants and Aya reference responses (Appendix A.4). Existing general instruction-following and healthcare coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds the sample-reweighting baseline IR-DRO for Llama and Mistral trained on Alpaca-52K. Its evaluation is explicitly restricted to those configurations. The existing NTP, biomedical-model, and data-selection comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: The experimental design expands to Qwen-2.5-14B on Alpaca, one-epoch Tulu3 training, and multilingual win/tie/loss evaluations judged by GPT-4o against Aya responses. New sensitivity settings include an α grid, μ = 0.05, and pairing the most/least confident thirds. Settings for retained experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's existing analyses, v3 adds α sensitivity, an additional μ setting, half-versus-third partition testing, a comparison of confidence dispersion, and an MT-Bench extraction case study (Section 4.1; Appendix A.1/A.3). The μ = 1 row in Table 9 repeats the existing Table 5 loss ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions report five instruction-following evaluation rounds and three medical QA evaluation rounds, without training-seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new 7% reduction in confidence-score standard deviation describes example-level dispersion, not uncertainty in performance estimates.

E6.justification: All matched scores in v2's Tables 1–9 are retained. v3 adds IR-DRO, Qwen, Tulu3, sensitivity, and multilingual results. For example, new Qwen NTP/SFTMix MT-Bench overall scores are 6.1930/6.5247; Chinese win rates are 30.4%/38.8% and French rates 34.5%/39.0%. These are additional comparisons, not improved versions of existing scores.

T1.justification: The gradient derivation from v2 Appendix A moves to v3 Section 3.4. Its equations and nonlinear-softmax argument remain substantively unchanged, as do the confidence and loss definitions. No new proof or formal result is introduced.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain confidence-guided Mixup regularization without requiring curated data, improved instruction-following and healthcare performance, and compatibility with data selection and constrained computation. Qwen and Tulu3 broaden the supporting examples; the shortened abstract and conclusion retain the central claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds confidence-dispersion and hyperparameter interpretations, discusses amortizing reference-model costs, and qualifies transfer and data-selection generality. It removes the English-only and untested safety-alignment caveats. Its new claim of larger Tulu3 gains across all metrics overstates Table 1: Mistral's within-dataset LC-WR improvement is 0.6210 on Tulu3 versus 0.9918 on UltraChat.

D1.justification: v3 documents Tulu3 training/preprocessing and the new multilingual data and judging choices, while retaining the original optimizer, hardware, and default hyperparameters. Table 10 introduces an inconsistent caption stating μ = 0.5, whereas Sections 4.1 and A.1 specify μ = 0.2 and α = 0.5. No SFTMix code-access information is added.

R1.justification: Related work adds IR-DRO and newer literature on data selection, preference optimization, and training-dynamics scaling, alongside sources for the new evaluations. The safety-alignment references disappear. These additions update coverage without changing the central positioning around confidence-aware data use and Mixup.

P1.justification: v3 shortens the abstract and conclusion, edits several explanatory paragraphs, and rewrites the limitations. The gradient appendix becomes Section 3.4, while experimental Appendix B becomes Appendix A and gains subsections. Most of the original narrative and section sequence remain.

P2.justification: The result displays expand substantially: Table 1 gains baseline, model, and dataset blocks; Table 9 expands; Tables 10–12 and qualitative Figure 4 are added. Figure 2 is rearranged and loses its enclosing border. Existing displays largely retain their content while being resized or repositioned.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the existing empirical case through IR-DRO comparisons, larger-model/data evaluations, Chinese/French tests, and α/partition ablations. These additions test generality and design choices more directly, while the limitations better acknowledge computational costs. The net gain is tempered by the overstated Tulu3 comparison, Table 10's inconsistent default-parameter caption, and removal of the untested safety-alignment limitation.
